Sarah Paine — Why wars are so difficult to end
result.description:
This is the final lecture in our series with Sarah Paine, and it's a fitting place to end.

Sarah tackles war termination: why wars are easy to start, hard to end, and even harder to end on the terms you wanted. Using the Russo-Japanese War as a model, she explains what goes wrong when regional wars escalate into global ones, or when conventional victories turn into endless insurgencies. It's especially relevant given what's going on today.

As we wrap up, I want to thank Sarah for doing this with me. It's been a real privilege to share her lectures with all of you. Thanks for watching.
